brief: Goldman's Financials and REITs desk reports a choppy week where sector outperformance diverged from investor mood. Three drivers moved stocks: hedge fund specialist positioning, macro/rates, and AI-driven growth sentiment, not earnings. A barbell of high-quality defensives (P&C insurance, card networks, senior housing REITs) and cheap/value risk-on names (regional banks, capital-light payments, lodging REITs, life insurance) outperformed, though life insurance began to leak late in the week as credit spreads and investment portfolios came back into focus. A large move lower in rates triggered a broad REIT rally even as earnings generally showed higher-rate-related activity pauses, broadly in line with buyside expectations. Most-debated earnings names: CBRE (underperformance magnitude debated around a surprise guide-down) and ZION (NII trends versus guide upside). MSCI and KRC worked on bullish feedback; BX moved opposite to majority feedback; SYF, AXP, FLG and FR fell in line with bearish feedback. MS is down 21% from highs on a "late-cycle" read, shifting bank-investor focus to excess capital versus peers. Next week's watch list spans card networks, insurance brokers, LPLA, AMP, COIN, REITs and credit alts, plus mortgage insurers shrugging off a regulatory overhang and SLM's -11% print as a possible consumer-credit warning sign.
